taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-a-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-07, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 2831.4 | 17.20 | 17.20
2 | 3567.9 | 2.07 | 19.27
3 | 3454.3 | 21.64 | 40.91
4 | 11701.4 | 4.12 | 45.03
5 | 140416.4 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as QHA-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-07, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Groundwater Site Note: Station T-07**

Station T-07 exhibits a 5-layer geoelectric model:
- **Layer 1:** 2,831.4 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$, thickness 17.20 m (depth: 0–17.20 m)
- **Layer 2:** 3,567.9 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$, thickness 2.07 m (depth: 17.20–19.27 m)
- **Layer 3:** 3,454.3 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$, thickness 21.64 m (depth: 19.27–40.91 m)
- **Layer 4:** 11,701.4 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$, thickness 4.12 m (depth: 40.91–45.03 m)
- **Layer 5:** 140,416.4 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$ (resistive basement)

Evaluation of consecutive layer triplets yields:
1. Layers 1–2–3: $r_1 < r_2 > r_3 \rightarrow \text{K}$
2. Layers 2–3–4: $r_2 > r_3 < r_4 \rightarrow \text{H}$
3. Layers 3–4–5: $r_3 < r_4 < r_5 \rightarrow \text{A}$

The resulting curve is **KHA-type**. The on-file classification of QHA-type is erroneous and does not match the interpreted layer sequence.

{"curve_type_stated": "QHA", "label_issue_flagged": true}
